chapters.title: Related ISO/IEC 42001 and EU AI Act note

recitals.title: Guidance on AI risk management, not a law
recitals.text: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 is voluntary guidance on risk management for artificial intelligence. It is not the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), not a prohibited-practices list, and not a high-risk conformity-assessment regime. Organizations may use it to structure AI risk processes. Buy the full text from ISO for the guidance clauses.

recitals.title: ISO 31000 overlay (catalogue and public comparisons)
recitals.text: ISO.org and public OECD comparisons describe ISO/IEC 23894 as guidance that uses ISO 31000 (Risk management — Guidelines) as the foundation and adds AI-specific considerations. ISO 31000’s well-known public process is: communication and consultation; scope, context and criteria; risk assessment (identify, analyse, evaluate); risk treatment; monitoring and review; recording and reporting. ISO/IEC 23894 applies that process to AI systems across their life cycle.

recitals.title: Related ISO/IEC 42001 is the certifiable AIMS
recitals.text: ISO/IEC 42001 is a related but distinct International Standard: an Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) that can be certified. ISO/IEC 23894 is guidance on AI risk management, not that certifiable MSS. This workspace maps 23894 (not 42001) as the AI Act analogue because the user asked for ISO 23894. Mentions of 42001 here are relationship notes only.

recitals.title: Closest international analogue to the EU AI Act — not a copy
recitals.text: This workspace maps ISO/IEC 23894 to the EU AI Act because both address AI risk, governance, and human oversight themes. The AI Act is binding Union law with prohibited practices, high-risk duties, GPAI rules, and market surveillance. ISO/IEC 23894 is committee guidance (JTC 1/SC 42, 26 pages, February 2023) for organizations developing, providing, or using AI. Use the AI Act instrument for Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

recitals.title: Copyright: educational overlay only
recitals.text: ISO owns the copyright in ISO/IEC 23894. This corpus uses public catalogue facts, the publicly known ISO 31000 process titles, and original educational notes (including OECD-published comparison themes such as governance, stakeholder engagement, human oversight, record-keeping, and re-assessment). It does not reproduce paid guidance paragraphs.

articles.title: Clause 1 — Scope (catalogue abstract)
articles.text: Public catalogue description: ISO/IEC 23894 provides guidance on how organizations that develop, produce, deploy or use products, systems and services that utilize artificial intelligence (AI) can manage risk specifically related to AI. It is intended to be used in connection with ISO 31000. Educational overlay — the paid document contains the full scope, exclusions, and examples.

articles.title: Relationship to ISO 31000
articles.text: ISO 31000:2018 is ISO’s generic risk-management guideline (principles, framework, process). ISO/IEC 23894 is an AI-specific overlay: it does not replace ISO 31000. Public process titles reused here: communication and consultation; establishing scope, context and criteria; risk identification, analysis and evaluation; risk treatment; monitoring and review; recording and reporting. AI adds model behaviour, data quality, and autonomy as risk sources.

articles.title: Organizational context for AI risk
articles.text: Before treating AI risk, an organization determines the internal and external context: which AI systems it develops or uses, who is affected, which legal regimes apply (for example the EU AI Act in the Union — a different instrument), and what risk criteria (severity, likelihood, human-rights impact) it will use. Context is an ISO 31000 step, specialized here to AI life cycles (design, training, deployment, monitoring, retirement).

articles.title: Leadership and AI governance (educational)
articles.text: Public comparisons of ISO/IEC 23894 with ISO 31000 note additional emphasis on governance for AI. In this educational map, leadership sets AI risk appetite, assigns accountability for models and data, and integrates AI risk into enterprise risk management. Governance is not an EU AI Act notified-body or CE-marking process.

articles.title: Stakeholder engagement and human oversight (educational)
articles.text: Public OECD-style comparisons highlight stakeholder engagement and human oversight as AI-specific additions to generic risk management. Affected people, users, and oversight staff need to be considered when identifying AI risk and when treating it (for example retaining meaningful human review of consequential outputs). This is guidance, not the AI Act’s high-risk human-oversight article.

articles.title: AI risk identification
articles.text: Risk identification asks what could go wrong because of an AI system: unsafe outputs, bias, privacy leakage, security of models and training data, loss of human control, environmental cost, or third-party model dependencies. Identification should cover the AI life cycle, not only production inference. Educational overlay using ISO 31000 process titles.

articles.title: AI risk analysis and evaluation
articles.text: Analysis estimates likelihood and consequence of identified AI risks; evaluation compares those levels to the organization’s criteria to decide which risks need treatment. AI-specific difficulty includes uncertainty of model behaviour on unseen data and systemic effects when many actors use similar models. Evaluation does not create the AI Act’s high-risk list in Annex III.

articles.title: AI risk treatment
articles.text: Treatment options follow ISO 31000: avoid, reduce, share, or retain risk. AI treatments commonly include data governance, evaluation and testing, access controls, human oversight, incident response, and contractual allocation with model providers. Residual risk should remain within appetite. This is management guidance, not a statutory conformity assessment.

articles.title: Monitoring, tracking, and record-keeping (educational)
articles.text: Public comparisons note extra emphasis on monitoring, tracking, and records for AI. Models drift; data pipelines change; new use cases appear. Organizations are expected to monitor deployed AI, keep records that support review, and report risk status to leadership. Records here are risk-management records, not AI Act technical documentation annexes.

articles.title: Continual improvement and re-assessment (educational)
articles.text: Public comparisons also note re-assessment: AI risk is not a one-time design-time exercise. After incidents, material model updates, or context changes, the organization repeats identification, analysis, evaluation, and treatment. Continual improvement closes the ISO 31000 cycle.

articles.title: Related ISO/IEC 42001 Artificial intelligence management system
articles.text: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies a certifiable Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS). Organizations that want a certifiable MSS for AI should look at 42001. ISO/IEC 23894 remains the risk-management guidance overlay on ISO 31000. They can be used together: 42001 for the management system, 23894 for how to run the risk process. This product does not currently ship a 42001 corpus.

articles.title: Not the EU Artificial Intelligence Act
articles.text: ISO/IEC 23894 does not prohibit AI practices, does not classify high-risk systems, does not regulate general-purpose AI models, and does not create an EU AI Office. The EU AI Act does those things as binding law. Mapping in this product is analogical (AI risk and governance). Use the AI Act instrument for Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
